title: No Verified Incident Can Excuse Dog-Trade Biosecurity Gaps
excerpt: No police seizure, court verdict, or health alert is documented here. That gap blocks honest mythbusting—and demands transparent records before reform.
body_html:
No verified police seizure, court verdict, cyanide-bait incident, or emergency health alert appears in this source record. That absence matters. Stolen companion animals, illegal transport, and unsafe slaughter require named records, dates, locations, and accountable agencies—not repeated claims.

Tradition cannot replace traceability

A lawful cultural practice does not excuse criminal theft, illegal transport, or regulatory breaches. Claims about “farm-raised dogs” need traceable farms, transport documents, veterinary inspection, quarantine records, and slaughter controls. No such records appear here. Without them, no honest account can prove that commercial supply chains rely on farms—or prove the opposite in any specific case.

Biosecurity demands facts, not slogans

Rabies control and dog-trade oversight are related public-safety concerns, but household exposure incidents must not be falsely presented as proof of commercial-trade transmission. Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance sets this medical standard.

Vietnamese communities deserve accountable reform

Families, pet guardians, veterinarians, public-health workers, and local reform leaders deserve records that withstand scrutiny. Agencies should publish seizure reports, court outcomes, quarantine findings, transport violations, and health alerts. Evidence must identify perpetrators and institutional failures without blaming Vietnamese people or lawful communities.

SDE calls for complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. This campaign demand differs from official public-health targets and cannot replace enforcement or medical care. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, then follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
